builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Attend at the Right Resolution: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention via Query-Key Interaction Structure
summary: HASA replaces dense attention and fixed-heuristic training-free sparse attention with head-specific selection: each head's query-key operator is compressed to an effective-rank response space, tokens are merged by directional coherence, and exact attention runs on the original KV states of selected regions. It requires no retraining but adds per-head singular-spectrum analysis, region-merging logic, and non-standard attention kernels or routing code, increasing inference-path complexity. It can fail if pretrained heads exhibit diffuse interaction structure (raising effective rank and erasing sparsity), if region merging discards critical tokens on out-of-distribution inputs, or if the 11.9% of missed attention mass degrades tasks sensitive to long-range rare dependencies; realized speedup also depends on hardware-efficient sparse kernels, which a single 24 GB GPU deployment may not yet have.
rationale: Training-free sparse attention is directly applicable to long-context inference on a single GPU, but the claimed gains are kernel- and workload-dependent and the method is new, so it warrants a controlled pilot against existing sparse-attention baselines before production adoption.

claims.statement: HASA replaces dense attention and fixed-heuristic training-free sparse attention with head-specific selection: each head's query-key operator is compressed to an effective-rank response space, tokens are merged by directional coherence, and exact attention runs on the original KV states of selected regions. It requires no retraining but adds per-head singular-spectrum analysis, region-merging logic, and non-standard attention kernels or routing code, increasing inference-path complexity. It can fail if pretrained heads exhibit diffuse interaction structure (raising effective rank and erasing sparsity), if region merging discards critical tokens on out-of-distribution inputs, or if the 11.9% of missed attention mass degrades tasks sensitive to long-range rare dependencies; realized speedup also depends on hardware-efficient sparse kernels, which a single 24 GB GPU deployment may not yet have.

Up to 1.32x self-attention speedup over the UNIQUE sparse-attention baseline and up to 14.07x over dense attention, while capturing 88.1% of dense-attention mass and improving accuracy by up to 3.47 points on RULER and 2.57 points on LongBench-Pro.
